manner.en: died of a chest gunshot wound
mortally wounded when a captured cannon burst

units.zh: 列傳二百二十二
units.en: Biographies 222
units.literal: Biographies 222

units.zh: 華爾勒伯勒東法爾第福戈登日意格德克碑赫德帛黎
units.en: Ward, Lebrethon, Foudrinière, Gordon, Giquel, von Sternberg, Hart, and Brière
units.literal: Ward, Lebrethon, Foudrinière, Gordon, Giquel, von Sternberg, Hart, and Brière

units.zh: 華爾，美國紐約人。
units.en: Ward was an American from New York.
units.literal: Ward was a native of New York in the United States.

units.zh: 嘗為其國將弁，以罪廢來上海，國人欲執之。
units.en: He had once served as an officer in the American army, but was dismissed for misconduct and fled to Shanghai, where his compatriots sought to seize him.
units.literal: He had once been an officer of his country, but was cashiered for a crime and came to Shanghai; his countrymen wished to arrest him.

units.zh: 會粵匪陷蘇州，上海籌防，謀練精兵。
units.en: When the Taiping rebels captured Suzhou, Shanghai organized its defenses and set out to drill a crack force.
units.literal: It happened that the Cantonese rebels took Suzhou; Shanghai made defensive preparations and planned to train elite troops.

units.zh: 蘇松太道吳煦識其才，言於美領事，獲免，以是德之，原效力，俾領印度兵。
units.en: Wu Xu, intendant of the Suzhou-Songjiang-Taicang circuit, recognized his ability, appealed to the American consul to spare him arrest, and won his lasting loyalty; Ward volunteered to serve and was put in command of Indian soldiers.
units.literal: The Suzhou-Songjiang-Taicang Circuit intendant Wu Xu recognized his talent, spoke to the American consul, and secured his release; in gratitude Ward offered his service and was made to command Indian troops.

units.zh: 既撤，自陳原隸中國。
units.en: When those Indian troops were withdrawn, he asked to enter Chinese service outright.
units.literal: After they were withdrawn, he declared of his own accord that he wished to enter Chinese service.

units.zh: 咸豐十年，粵匪陷松江，煦令募西兵數十為前驅；
units.en: In 1860 the rebels took Songjiang, and Xu ordered Ward to recruit several dozen Western soldiers as the vanguard;
units.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels took Songjiang; Xu ordered several dozen Western soldiers recruited as vanguard;

units.zh: 華人數百，半西服、半常裝，從其後。
units.en: with several hundred Chinese behind them, half in Western uniform and half in ordinary clothes.
units.literal: several hundred Chinese followed behind, half in Western dress and half in ordinary dress.

units.zh: 華爾誡曰：「有進無止，止者斬！」
units.en: Ward warned his men: "Keep moving forward—anyone who stops will be executed!"
units.literal: Ward warned them, saying, "Advance without halt; whoever halts shall be beheaded!"

units.zh: 賊迎戰，槍砲雨下，令伏，無一傷者。
units.en: The rebels met them with a storm of musket and cannon fire; Ward ordered his men to drop flat, and not one was hit.
units.literal: The rebels met them in battle; guns and cannon rained down, but he ordered his men to lie low, and not one was wounded.

units.zh: 俄突起轟擊之，百二十槍齊發，凡三發，斃賊數百。
units.en: Then they sprang up and opened fire; one hundred and twenty rifles discharged in three volleys, killing several hundred rebels.
units.literal: Then suddenly they rose and blasted the enemy; one hundred and twenty guns fired together, three volleys in all, and several hundred rebels were killed.

units.zh: 賊敗入城，躡之同入，巷戰，斬黃衣賊數人。
units.en: The rebels broke and retreated into the city; Ward followed them in, fought street by street, and killed several of their yellow-coated officers.
units.literal: The rebels were defeated and fled into the city; Ward pursued them inside, fought in the lanes, and cut down several rebels in yellow coats.

units.zh: 賊遁走，遂復松江，華爾亦被創。
units.en: The rebels fled, Songjiang was retaken, and Ward himself was wounded in the fight.
units.literal: The rebels fled, and Songjiang was recovered; Ward was also wounded.

units.zh: 先是煦與華爾約，城克，罄賊所有以予。
units.en: Xu had earlier promised Ward that if the city fell, Ward would receive everything the rebels left behind.
units.literal: Earlier Xu and Ward had agreed that when the city was taken, everything the rebels possessed would be given to Ward.

units.zh: 至是入賊館，空無所得，以五千金酬之。
units.en: When they entered the rebel headquarters they found nothing of value, so Xu paid him five thousand taels of silver instead.
units.literal: On this occasion they entered the rebel quarters and found nothing; five thousand taels of silver were paid him as reward instead.

units.zh: 令守松江，又募練洋槍隊五百，服裝器械步伐皆效西人。
units.en: Ward was left to hold Songjiang and raised five hundred more men for a foreign-rifle corps, trained in Western dress, arms, and drill.
units.literal: He was ordered to garrison Songjiang and again recruited and drilled five hundred men in the foreign-rifle corps; dress, weapons, and marching all imitated Westerners.

units.zh: 同治元年，賊又犯松江富林、塘橋，眾數万，直偪城下。
units.en: In 1862 the rebels struck Fulins and Tangqiao near Songjiang with a host of tens of thousands and drove straight against the city.
units.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi the rebels again attacked Fulins and Tangqiao in Songjiang; their force numbered tens of thousands and pressed straight to the foot of the walls.

units.zh: 華爾以五百人御之，被圍，乃分其眾為數圓陣，陣五重，人四鄉，最內者平立，以次遞俯，槍皆外指。
units.en: Ward met them with five hundred men, was surrounded, and formed several concentric circles five ranks deep, the inner ranks standing upright and the outer ranks kneeling in turn, every rifle pointed outward.
units.literal: Ward with five hundred men opposed them and was surrounded; he then divided his force into several circular formations, five ranks deep, men facing four directions; those innermost stood upright, those farther out stooped in succession, all guns pointing outward.

units.zh: 華爾居中吹角，一響眾應，三發，死賊數百。
units.en: Ward stood at the center and blew his bugle; at one call the whole line fired three volleys and killed several hundred rebels.
units.literal: Ward stood in the center and blew the horn; at one blast all answered; three volleys were fired and several hundred rebels died.

units.zh: 逐北辰山，再被創，力疾與戰，賊始退。
units.en: He pursued them to Beichen Hill, was wounded a second time, yet fought on through his injuries until the rebels finally broke off.
units.literal: He pursued them to Beichen Hill, was wounded again, fought on despite illness, and the rebels at last withdrew.

units.zh: 遂會諸軍搗敵營，殺守門者，爭先入毀之。
units.en: He then joined the government forces in storming the rebel camp, killed the gate guards, and led the rush to break in and destroy it.
units.literal: He then joined the other armies in storming the enemy camp, killed the gate guards, and vied to enter first and destroy it.

units.zh: 是役也，以寡敵眾，稱奇捷。
units.en: In this fight a small force had routed a great one, and the victory was hailed as extraordinary.
units.literal: In this battle, with few against many, it was acclaimed a remarkable victory.

units.zh: 時浦東賊據高橋，偪上海，華爾約英、法兵守海濱，而自率所部進擊，賊大敗，加四品翎頂。
units.en: Rebels on the Pudong shore held Gaoqiao and menaced Shanghai; Ward posted British and French troops along the coast while he led his own men in a assault that routed the enemy, for which he was awarded the fourth-rank peacock feather.
units.literal: At the time rebels on the east bank of the Huangpu held Gaoqiao and threatened Shanghai; Ward arranged for British and French troops to guard the coast while he himself led his unit in attack; the rebels were heavily defeated, and he was given the fourth-rank peacock feather.

units.zh: 會李鴻章帥師至滬，乃隸戲下，令立常勝軍，益募兵三千俾教練，參將李恆嵩副之，餉倍發。
units.en: When Li Hongzhang brought his army to Shanghai, Ward entered his service; Li formed the Ever Victorious Army, added three thousand recruits for Ward to drill, appointed Assistant General Li Hengsong as his second, and doubled the corps' pay.
units.literal: When Li Hongzhang arrived at Shanghai in command of an army, Ward entered his service; Li ordered the Ever Victorious Army established, increased recruitment by three thousand men for Ward to train, with Assistant General Li Hengsong as his deputy, and pay was doubled.

units.zh: 賊據王家寺，與英提督何伯等合攻。
units.en: The rebels held Wangjia Temple, and Ward attacked it jointly with British Admiral Hope and his forces.
units.literal: The rebels held Wangjia Temple; Ward joined the British admiral Hope and others in the attack.

units.zh: 華爾賈勇先入，大斬虜首，進偪南翔，賊亦悉眾轟拒，何伯負傷。
units.en: Ward led the charge and cut down many rebels, then pressed toward Nanxiang; the enemy met him with their full artillery, and Hope was wounded.
units.literal: Ward with fierce courage entered first and cut down many of the enemy; pressing on toward Nanxiang, the rebels also brought out their full strength in cannon fire to resist, and Hope was wounded.

units.zh: 華爾冒煙直進，立毀其營，生獲八百餘人，遂復嘉定。
units.en: Ward pushed straight through the smoke, overran the camp at once, took more than eight hundred prisoners, and retook Jiading.
units.literal: Ward advanced straight through the smoke, immediately destroyed their camp, took more than eight hundred alive, and thus recovered Jiading.

units.zh: 規取青浦，華爾略東門，城潰；
units.en: In the drive on Qingpu, Ward assaulted the east gate and the wall gave way;
units.literal: Planning to take Qingpu, Ward attacked by the east gate and the wall collapsed;

units.zh: 英、法兵自西入，華爾為承。
units.en: British and French troops entered from the west while Ward supported them.
units.literal: British and French troops entered from the west, with Ward in support.

units.zh: 賊奔，爭赴水死。
units.en: The rebels fled, many throwing themselves into the water to drown.
units.literal: The rebels fled and many rushed into the water to their deaths.

units.zh: 攻奉賢，法提督卜羅德遇害，詔賞貂皮採絨，卹其家。
units.en: During the assault on Fengxian the French Admiral Protet was killed; the court granted his family sable furs, colored silks, and posthumous honors.
units.literal: In the attack on Fengxian, the French admiral Protet was killed; an edict awarded sable fur and colored silk and granted relief to his family.

units.zh: 時恆嵩扼趙屯港、四江口，屢失利，嘉、青复危。
units.en: Li Hengsong held Zhaotun Harbor and Sikou River but met repeated defeats, and Jiading and Qingpu were threatened once more.
units.literal: At the time Hengsong held Zhaotun Harbor and Sikou River but suffered repeated defeats; Jiading and Qingpu were again in peril.

units.zh: 華爾方議直搗金山衛，聞敗，還守青浦。
units.en: Ward had been planning a direct strike on Jinshanwei when news of the defeat reached him, and he fell back to defend Qingpu.
units.literal: Ward was just discussing a direct strike on Jinshanwei when he heard of the defeat and returned to hold Qingpu.

units.zh: 而富林、泗涇又相繼失，乃棄青浦，簡壯士五百襲天馬山，破之。
units.en: Fulins and Sijing fell in turn, so he abandoned Qingpu, picked five hundred picked men, stormed Tianma Hill, and routed the rebels there.
units.literal: Fulins and Sijing were lost in succession; he then abandoned Qingpu, selected five hundred stalwart men, raided Tianma Hill, and broke the enemy there.

units.zh: 入城挈守軍出，並力守松江，登陴轟擊兩晝夜不絕，賊宵遁，圍解。
units.en: He entered the city, led the garrison out, and with combined forces held Songjiang; from the walls they shelled the enemy without pause for two days and nights until the rebels slipped away at night and the siege was raised.
units.literal: He entered the city, brought out the garrison, and together they defended Songjiang; mounting the walls they blasted the enemy for two days and nights without cease; the rebels fled by night and the siege was lifted.

units.zh: 官軍圖青浦，華爾攻南門，駕輪舶入濠，毀城十餘丈，麾眾登堞，賊鬥且走，追敗之白鶴江黃渡，復其城，晉副將銜，降敕褒賞。
units.en: When the government forces moved on Qingpu, Ward assaulted the south gate, brought a steamer into the moat, breached more than thirty feet of wall, and led his men onto the ramparts; the rebels fought a fighting retreat; he pursued and routed them at Baihe River and Huangdu, retook the city, was promoted to vice general, and received an imperial commendation.
units.literal: The government armies aimed at Qingpu; Ward attacked the south gate, drove a steam vessel into the moat, destroyed more than ten zhang of wall, ordered his men onto the battlements; the rebels fought as they fled; pursuing them he defeated them at Baihe River and Huangdu, recovered the city, was promoted to vice general's rank, and received an imperial decree of praise and reward.

units.zh: 俄偽慕王譚紹光復來犯，薄西門，與總兵黃翼升各軍擊之，賊潰，奔北岸，華爾毀其七營。
units.en: Soon the Taiping commander Tan Shaoguang attacked again and pressed the west gate; Ward joined Major General Huang Yisheng's forces in driving the rebels back across the north bank and destroying seven of their camps.
units.literal: Soon the false Prince of Mu Tan Shaoguang came again to attack, pressing the west gate; with Major General Huang Yisheng and the various armies he struck them; the rebels were routed, fled to the north bank, and Ward destroyed their seven camps.

units.zh: 踰月，會西兵再复嘉定。
units.en: A month later he joined the Western forces in retaking Jiading once more.
units.literal: After more than a month, he joined Western troops in recovering Jiading again.

units.zh: 其秋，賊十萬复犯上海，華爾自松江倍道應赴，與諸軍擊卻之。
units.en: That autumn a rebel host of one hundred thousand struck at Shanghai again; Ward rushed from Songjiang by forced marches and, with the other armies, beat them off.
units.literal: That autumn one hundred thousand rebels again attacked Shanghai; Ward from Songjiang marched by forced stages to answer the call and, with the other armies, drove them back.

units.zh: 時寧波戒嚴，巡道史致諤乞援，鴻章遣華爾偕往。
units.en: Ningbo was then under martial law; Circuit Intendant Shi Zhi'e appealed for help, and Li Hongzhang dispatched Ward to his aid.
units.literal: At the time Ningbo was on alert; Circuit Intendant Shi Zhi'e begged for aid, and Hongzhang sent Ward to go with him.

units.zh: 值廣艇與法兵構釁，引賊寇新城，從姚北紆道犯慈谿。
units.en: Just then Cantonese river boats and French troops clashed, drawing rebels against Xincheng; the enemy then looped north of Yuyao and struck at Cixi.
units.literal: It happened that Guangdong boats and French troops clashed; this drew rebels to raid Xincheng, and by a roundabout route north of Yuyao they attacked Cixi.

units.zh: 華爾約西兵駕輪舶三，一泊灌浦，一泊赭山，一自丈亭駛入太平橋、餘姚四門鎮，而自率軍數百至半浦。
units.en: Ward coordinated three steamers with Western troops: one at Guanpu, one at Zhushan, and one sailing from Zhangting toward Taiping Bridge and Simen in Yuyao, while he led several hundred men to Banpu.
units.literal: Ward arranged for Western troops to man three steam vessels: one moored at Guanpu, one at Zhushan, and one to sail from Zhangting into Taiping Bridge and Yuyao's Simen Town, while he himself led several hundred men to Banpu.

units.zh: 平旦薄城，方以遠鏡了敵，忽槍丸洞胸，遽踣地，舁回舟。
units.en: At dawn he closed on the city walls; as he was studying the enemy through his telescope, a bullet pierced his chest and he collapsed; his men carried him back to the boat.
units.literal: At dawn he pressed the city; just as he was surveying the enemy through a telescope, a bullet pierced his chest; he suddenly fell to the ground and was carried back to the boat.

units.zh: 餘眾悉力奮攻，賊啟北門走。
units.en: His men pressed the assault with all their strength, and the rebels opened the north gate and fled.
units.literal: The rest of the force attacked with all their strength; the rebels opened the north gate and fled.

units.zh: 華爾至郡城，猶能叱其下卹軍事，越二日始卒。
units.en: Ward was brought to the prefectural seat and still gave orders about military affairs; he died two days later.
units.literal: Ward reached the prefectural city and could still command his subordinates to attend to military affairs; only after two days did he die.

units.zh: 以中國章服斂，從其志也。
units.en: He was buried in Chinese official robes, as he had wished.
units.literal: He was buried in Chinese official dress, in accordance with his wish.

units.zh: 鴻章請於朝，優恤之，予寧波、松江建祠。
units.en: Li Hongzhang memorialized the throne for generous posthumous honors and for temples to be built in his memory at Ningbo and Songjiang.
units.literal: Hongzhang memorialized the court for generous posthumous favor and permission to build temples to him at Ningbo and Songjiang.

units.zh: 初，喪歸，煦檢其篋，得金陵城圖，賊所居處及城垣丈尺方位纖悉畢具，論者頗稱其機密雲。
units.en: When Ward's body was brought back, Xu examined his trunk and found a detailed map of Nanjing showing rebel quarters and the exact dimensions and layout of the walls; contemporaries praised his remarkable intelligence work.
units.literal: Earlier, when the coffin returned, Xu searched his trunk and found a map of Jinling city, with the rebels' quarters and the city walls' dimensions and positions all set out in minute detail; commentators greatly praised his secret intelligence.

units.zh: 勒伯勒東德加理尼阿爾伯依都額爾，法國加爾襪多人。
units.en: Lebrethon (de Galerny, Albert Edward) was from Calvados in France.
units.literal: Lebrethon, de Galerny, Albert Edward, was a native of Calvados in France.

units.zh: 初為本國水師參將。
units.en: He had first served as a staff captain in the French navy.
units.literal: He had first been a staff captain in his country's navy.

units.zh: 咸豐十一年，來上海。
units.en: He came to Shanghai in 1861.
units.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng he came to Shanghai.

units.zh: 時寇據寧波，西人惡之，益兵戍守，遣勒伯勒東乘輪泊三江口。
units.en: Rebels then held Ningbo; the Western powers, hostile to them, reinforced their garrisons and sent Lebrethon by steamer to anchor at the mouth of the Yong River.
units.literal: At the time bandits held Ningbo; Westerners detested them, increased troops for garrison duty, and sent Lebrethon by steamer to anchor at Sanjiangkou.

units.zh: 同治元年，從官軍克府城，募壯丁千五百為洋槍隊，自陳願隸。
units.en: In 1862 he joined the government forces in recovering the prefectural seat, raised fifteen hundred men for a foreign-rifle corps, and volunteered to serve under Chinese command.
units.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed the government army in taking the prefectural city, recruited fifteen hundred stalwart men for a foreign-rifle corps, and declared of his own accord that he wished to enter their service.

units.zh: 明年，權授浙江總兵，受巡撫、寧波道節度。
units.en: The following year he was made acting major general of Zhejiang and placed under the governor and the Ningbo intendant.
units.literal: The next year he was provisionally appointed major general of Zhejiang and placed under the command of the governor and the Ningbo circuit intendant.

units.zh: 時上虞賊犯泗門、馬渚，勒伯勒東軍餘姚以待。
units.en: When rebels from Shangyu struck Simen and Mazhu, Lebrethon encamped at Yuyao to meet them.
units.literal: At the time rebels from Shangyu attacked Simen and Mazhu; Lebrethon stationed his army at Yuyao to await them.

units.zh: 尋與同知銜謝採嶂直搗賊屯，賊赴水死者千餘，乘銳毀其卡，薄城先登，擊殺守陴悍賊，餘宵遁，城克。
units.en: He soon joined Associate Prefect Xie Caizhang in a direct assault on the rebel camp; more than a thousand rebels drowned; pressing the attack he destroyed their barricades, was first up the wall, and killed the defenders; the rest fled by night and the city fell.
units.literal: Soon, with Associate Prefect Xie Caizhang, he struck straight at the rebel encampment; more than a thousand rebels died in the water; pressing the advantage he destroyed their stockades, pressed the city and mounted first, killed fierce rebels on the walls; the rest fled by night and the city was taken.

units.zh: 赴蟶浦，略紹興，以賊遺土砲往，巡道張景渠止之，不聽，未幾，砲果裂，負傷而死，賜優恤。
units.en: He marched on Chengpu and raided Shaoxing, bringing along a captured rebel field gun; Circuit Intendant Zhang Jingqu tried to dissuade him, but he refused; the gun soon burst, mortally wounding him, and the court granted him generous posthumous honors.
units.literal: He went to Chengpu and raided Shaoxing, taking along a captured earth cannon left by the rebels; Circuit Intendant Zhang Jingqu tried to stop him but he would not listen; before long the cannon indeed burst; he was wounded and died, and generous posthumous favor was granted.

units.zh: 以法參將法爾第福為江蘇副將，領其軍，退守百官。
units.en: The French staff captain Foudrinière was appointed vice general of Jiangsu, took over the corps, and fell back to hold Baiguan.
units.literal: The French staff captain Foudrinière was made vice general of Jiangsu, took command of the army, and withdrew to garrison Baiguan.

units.zh: 法爾第福，又名買忒勒，頗讀華書。
units.en: Foudrinière, also known as Maitele, was well versed in Chinese literature.
units.literal: Foudrinière, also called Maitele, had read Chinese books extensively.

units.zh: 後攻紹興，焚西郭門。
units.en: He later attacked Shaoxing and burned the west suburb gate.
units.literal: Later he attacked Shaoxing and burned the west suburb gate.

units.zh: 次日復戰，潰十餘丈，麾眾登城，賊殊死鬥，別有黑種人數十助之，遂遇害。
units.en: The next day he renewed the assault, breached more than thirty feet of wall, and led his men onto the ramparts; the rebels fought desperately, aided by several dozen African soldiers, and he was killed in the fight.
units.literal: The next day he fought again, breached more than ten zhang of wall, ordered his men onto the wall; the rebels fought to the death, and several dozen black men separately aided them; he was then killed.

units.zh: 優恤之。
units.en: The court granted him generous posthumous honors.
units.literal: Generous posthumous favor was granted him.

units.zh: 戈登，英國人。
units.en: Gordon was a Briton.
units.literal: Gordon was an Englishman.

units.zh: 同治二年，李鴻章檄領常勝軍二千攻常州、福山營。
units.en: In 1863 Li Hongzhang ordered him to take two thousand Ever Victorious Army troops against the rebel camps at Changzhou and Fushan.
units.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang ordered him to lead two thousand men of the Ever Victorious Army to attack the Changzhou and Fushan camps.

units.zh: 別遣呂宋兵乘小舟薄賊壘，支木橋，伏死士城牆下。
units.en: He also sent Filipino troops in small boats against the rebel stockade, laid wooden bridges, and posted picked men beneath the wall.
units.literal: He separately sent Filipino troops in small boats to press the rebel stockade, set up wooden bridges, and posted death-defying men below the wall.

units.zh: 日中，港東西賊營皆破，緣牆入，痛殲之，遂奪福山石城。
units.en: By midday the rebel camps on both sides of the harbor were overrun; his men scaled the wall and cut the enemy down, seizing the stone fort at Fushan.
units.literal: At midday the rebel camps east and west of the harbor were all broken; climbing along the wall they entered and slaughtered them severely, and thus took the Fushan stone fort.

units.zh: 圍解，權授江蘇總兵。
units.en: The siege was raised, and he was made acting major general of Jiangsu.
units.literal: The siege was lifted, and he was provisionally appointed major general of Jiangsu.

units.zh: 進攻太倉，毀南門賊卡，戈登轟潰二石壘，官軍繼進，克之。
units.en: In the advance on Taicang they destroyed the rebel barricade at the south gate; Gordon shelled and shattered two stone forts, the government troops pressed on, and the city fell.
units.literal: Advancing to attack Taicang, they destroyed the rebel stockade at the south gate; Gordon blasted and broke two stone forts, the government army followed up, and the place was taken.

units.zh: 規取崑山，與總兵程學啟度地勢，以環昆多水，惟西南通進義，策先斷其歸路。
units.en: Planning the capture of Kunshan, he and Major General Cheng Xueqi studied the ground; water encircled the city on nearly every side, with only a southwest route to Jinyi, so they resolved to cut the rebels' retreat first.
units.literal: Planning to take Kunshan, he and Major General Cheng Xueqi surveyed the terrain; as Kunshan was ringed by much water and only the southwest connected with Jinyi, they planned first to cut off the enemy's line of retreat.

units.zh: 遂與駕輪舶以偏師繞而西，賊不虞其至也，即時敗奔，奪其四壘。
units.en: He took a steamer with a flanking force around to the west; the rebels were caught unprepared, broke at once, and lost four forts.
units.literal: He then took a steamer with a detached force and circled to the west; the rebels did not expect his arrival and at once fled in defeat; four of their forts were taken.

units.zh: 譚紹光構悍賊來爭，與諸軍大破之，薄昆城，偕李恆嵩夾擊，賊酋偽朝將先期逸去。
units.en: Tan Shaoguang rallied fierce rebel troops to meet them; Gordon and the allied armies routed them, closed on Kunshan, and with Li Hengsong attacked from both sides while the rebel commander, the false Court General, had already fled.
units.literal: Tan Shaoguang mustered fierce rebels to contest the ground; with the various armies he inflicted a great defeat, pressed Kunshan city, and with Li Hengsong attacked from both sides; the rebel chieftain, the false Court General, had already slipped away beforehand.

units.zh: 踰月，學啟攻東城，戈登自果浦河奄至，扼守西路，分道疾攻。
units.en: A month later Xueqi assaulted the east wall while Gordon came up swiftly along the Guopu River, sealed the western approach, and both columns pressed the attack.
units.literal: After more than a month, Xueqi attacked the east wall; Gordon from Guopu River came up suddenly, held the west road, and they attacked swiftly by separate routes.

units.zh: 賊奪西門走，阻水，殲焉。
units.en: The rebels broke out through the west gate but were trapped by the water and wiped out.
units.literal: The rebels seized the west gate and fled, were blocked by water, and were annihilated.

units.zh: 遂留駐昆城，策應各路。
units.en: He then garrisoned Kunshan to support operations on every front.
units.literal: He then remained stationed at Kunshan city to coordinate support for the various routes.

units.zh: 移師攻花涇港，知賊必不誡，率眾擊北門，毀城外賊壘。
units.en: He moved against Huajing Harbor, expecting the rebels to be unprepared; he struck the north gate and destroyed their outworks.
units.literal: He shifted his army to attack Huajing Harbor, knowing the rebels would certainly be off guard; he led his force against the north gate and destroyed the rebel forts outside the wall.

units.zh: 次日，賊降，收吳江、震澤而還。
units.en: The rebels surrendered the next day; he secured Wujiang and Zhenze and marched back.
units.literal: The next day the rebels surrendered; he recovered Wujiang and Zhenze and returned.

units.zh: 以事謁鴻章於上海。
units.en: He went to Shanghai on business to see Li Hongzhang.
units.literal: On business he called on Hongzhang at Shanghai.

units.zh: 先是白齊文閉松城索餉，既撤，潛通賊，領二百人入蘇州。
units.en: Earlier Burgevine had barricaded himself in Songjiang to demand back pay; after his removal he secretly dealt with the rebels and led two hundred men into Suzhou.
units.literal: Earlier Burgevine had shut himself in Songjiang city to demand pay; after he was removed, he secretly communicated with the rebels and led two hundred men into Suzhou.

units.zh: 戈登诇知之，亟返崑山為備。
units.en: Gordon learned of this through his scouts and hurried back to Kunshan to prepare.
units.literal: Gordon learned of it through reconnaissance and hastened back to Kunshan to prepare.

units.zh: 旋攻蘇城，率軍三千，與學啟俱力爭要害，稍剪城外賊壘。
units.en: He soon besieged Suzhou with three thousand men; he and Xueqi fought for every strong point and gradually reduced the outworks.
units.literal: Soon he attacked Suzhou city, leading three thousand troops; with Xueqi he both strove for key points and gradually cut down the rebel forts outside the wall.

units.zh: 偽忠王李秀成聞警赴援，屢敗；
units.en: The Taiping Prince of Zhong, Li Xiucheng, hurried to relieve the city and was beaten back again and again;
units.literal: The false Prince of Zhong Li Xiucheng, hearing the alarm, came to aid and was repeatedly defeated;

units.zh: 而紹光所部每戰猶致死，自偽納王郜雲官以下，皆萌貳志，詣營乞降。
units.en: yet Shaoguang's men still fought with desperate courage; from the false Prince of Na, Gao Yunguan, downward, the garrison turned toward surrender and sent envoys to the besiegers.
units.literal: yet Shaoguang's troops still fought to the death in every battle; from the false Prince of Na Gao Yunguan downward, all conceived thoughts of defection and came to the camp to beg surrender.

units.zh: 乃與學啟乘單舸會雲官等於洋澄湖，令斬秀成、紹光以獻，學啟與誓，戈登證之。
units.en: He and Xueqi then took a small boat to meet Yunguan and the others on Yangcheng Lake, demanding the heads of Xiucheng and Shaoguang as the price of surrender; Xueqi swore the pact and Gordon witnessed it.
units.literal: He then with Xueqi took a single boat to meet Yunguan and others at Yangcheng Lake, ordering them to behead Xiucheng and Shaoguang as proof; Xueqi swore an oath with them, and Gordon witnessed it.

units.zh: 未幾，秀成遁，雲官殺紹光，開齊門迎降，賞頭等功牌、銀幣，並犒其軍。
units.en: Xiucheng soon escaped; Yunguan killed Shaoguang, opened the Qi Gate to the besiegers, and was rewarded with a first-class merit plaque, silver, and a feast for his troops.
units.literal: Before long Xiucheng escaped; Yunguan killed Shaoguang, opened the Qi Gate to welcome surrender, and was rewarded with a first-class merit plaque and silver coins, and his army was also feasted.

units.zh: 助攻宜興、溧陽，並擊退楊舍賊。
units.en: He helped take Yixing and Liyang and drove off the rebels at Yangshe.
units.literal: He assisted in the attacks on Yixing and Liyang and also drove back the rebels at Yangshe.

units.zh: 進規常州，轟破南門，合諸軍掘壕築牆以敗之。
units.en: In the advance on Changzhou he shelled open the south gate and, with the allied armies, dug trenches and built siege lines to bring the city down.
units.literal: Advancing against Changzhou, he blasted open the south gate; with the various armies he dug trenches and built walls to defeat them.

units.zh: 敘功，賞黃馬褂、花翎，賜提督品級章服。
units.en: For his services he was awarded the yellow jacket and peacock feather and the dress of a provincial commander.
units.literal: His merit was recorded; he was awarded a yellow jacket and peacock feather and granted the insignia and robes of provincial commander rank.

units.zh: 初，戈登與學啟為昆弟交，每戰必偕。
units.en: Gordon and Xueqi had been as close as brothers and fought side by side in every engagement.
units.literal: At first Gordon and Xueqi were as close as brothers and fought together in every battle.

units.zh: 及誅降酋，頗不直其所為，捧雲官首而哭，誓不與見。
units.en: When the surrendered chiefs were put to death, he was deeply offended; he took Yunguan's head in his hands and wept, and swore never to see Xueqi again.
units.literal: When the surrendered chieftains were executed, he strongly disapproved of the act, took Yunguan's head in his hands and wept, and swore never to see Xueqi again.

units.zh: 嗣聞學啟卒，悲不自勝，乞其戰時大旗二，攜歸國為遺念。
units.en: When he later heard that Xueqi had died, he was overcome with grief and asked for two of his battle flags to take home as keepsakes.
units.literal: Later, hearing that Xueqi had died, he was overcome with grief beyond bearing; he begged for two of his battle flags and carried them home to his country as mementos.

units.zh: 戈登歸後，埃及亂，督師討之，遇害。
units.en: After Gordon returned home, rebellion broke out in Egypt; he led a punitive expedition there and was killed.
units.literal: After Gordon returned, Egypt was in revolt; he commanded an expedition against it and was killed.

units.zh: 朝廷遣使往吊焉。
units.en: The Qing court sent an envoy to convey its condolences.
units.literal: The court sent an envoy to offer condolences.

units.zh: 戈登嘗言：「中國人民耐勞易使，果能教練，可轉弱為強。」
units.en: Gordon once said, "The Chinese are hardy and obedient; properly trained, they could turn weakness into strength."
units.literal: Gordon once said: "The Chinese people are enduring in labor and easy to command; if they can truly be drilled, weakness can be turned into strength."

units.zh: 又曰：「中國海軍利於守，船砲之制，大不如小。」
units.en: He also said, "China's navy is best suited to defense; in warships and guns, smaller is better than larger."
units.literal: He also said: "China's navy is suited to defense; in the design of ships and cannon, large is far inferior to small."

units.zh: 當時稱其將略云。
units.en: Contemporaries praised his military judgment.
units.literal: At the time he was praised for his generalship.

units.zh: 日意格，法國人。
units.en: Giquel was French.
units.literal: Giquel was a Frenchman.

units.zh: 嘗為其國參將，駐防上海。
units.en: He had served as a French staff captain in the garrison at Shanghai.
units.literal: He had been a staff captain of his country, garrisoned at Shanghai.

units.zh: 同治元年，改調稅務司。
units.en: In 1862 he was transferred to the customs service.
units.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was transferred to serve as customs commissioner.

units.zh: 徙寧波，复郡城，與有功。
units.en: He went to Ningbo, took part in recovering the prefectural seat, and earned a share of the credit.
units.literal: He moved to Ningbo, recovered the prefectural city, and shared in the merit.

units.zh: 官軍攻慈谿，遣法兵馳往策應。
units.en: When government forces attacked Cixi, Giquel sent French troops to reinforce them.
units.literal: When the government army attacked Cixi, Giquel dispatched French troops to hurry there in support.

units.zh: 會餘姚四​​門鎮陷，遂與前護提督陳世章勒兵往討，踰月，直搗上虞。
units.en: When Simen in Yuyao fell, he joined Acting Provincial Commander Chen Shizhang in a month-long campaign that drove straight at Shangyu.
units.literal: It happened that Simen Town in Yuyao fell; he then with Acting Provincial Commander Chen Shizhang led troops to punish the rebels; after more than a month they struck straight at Shangyu.

units.zh: 賊緣道築卡樹柵，悉奪毀之，薄城，並力轟擊，賊殊死戰，賈勇直前，被創，眾軍繼進，斬級千，賊始渡曹娥江去。
units.en: They destroyed every rebel barricade along the road, closed on the city, and shelled it together; the rebels resisted desperately; Giquel led a bold charge and was wounded, but the main force followed, took a thousand heads, and drove the enemy across the Cao'e River.
units.literal: The rebels built stockades and palisades along the road; all were seized and destroyed; pressing the city they blasted together; the rebels fought to the death; with fierce courage he pressed forward, was wounded, the main army followed up, heads cut numbered a thousand, and the rebels at last crossed the Cao'e River and left.

units.zh: 進攻奉化，與諸軍克之。
units.en: He advanced on Fenghua and, with the allied armies, captured it.
units.literal: He advanced to attack Fenghua and, with the various armies, took it.

units.zh: 攻安吉思溪、雙福橋，駕小輪舶赴荻港，毀袁家匯賊壘，浙江平。
units.en: He attacked Anji, Jixi, and Shuangfu Bridge, took a small steamer to Dih Harbor, destroyed the rebel stronghold at Yuanjia Hui, and Zhejiang was pacified.
units.literal: He attacked Anji, Jixi, and Shuangfu Bridge, drove a small steamer to Dih Harbor, destroyed the rebel fort at Yuanjia Hui, and Zhejiang was pacified.

units.zh: 左宗棠令與德克碑討測西邦製造，仿造小輪舶試行。
units.en: Zuo Zongtang had him and von Sternberg study Western shipbuilding and build experimental steam launches.
units.literal: Zuo Zongtang ordered him and von Sternberg to investigate Western manufacturing methods and trial-build small steam vessels.

units.zh: 五年，宗棠創福州船政局，充正監督，度地募工，殫心所事；
units.en: In 1866 Zuo founded the Foochow Naval Dockyard; Giquel became chief superintendent, chose the site, recruited labor, and gave himself entirely to the work;
units.literal: In the fifth year Zongtang founded the Foochow Naval Dockyard; Giquel served as chief superintendent, surveyed the site and recruited workers, and devoted his whole heart to the task;

units.zh: 复籌設繪事院、小鐵廠。
units.en: He also set up a drafting school and a small iron foundry.
units.literal: He also planned and established a drafting school and a small ironworks.

units.zh: 七年，加提督銜，賞花翎。
units.en: In 1868 he received provincial commander rank and the peacock feather.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was given provincial commander rank and awarded the peacock feather.

units.zh: 十三年，以船政教導勞賞銀幣。
units.en: In 1874 he was rewarded with silver for his service in training the dockyard.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, for his labor in instructing the dockyard, he was rewarded with silver coins.

units.zh: 光緒年，卒。
units.en: He died during the Guangxu reign.
units.literal: In the Guangxu reign he died.

units.zh: 德克碑，法參將。
units.en: Von Sternberg was a French staff captain.
units.literal: Von Sternberg was a French staff captain.

units.zh: 初，助攻奉化有功。
units.en: He first distinguished himself in the capture of Fenghua.
units.literal: At first, in the joint attack on Fenghua, he had merit.

units.zh: 旋奉其公使檄，將受代歸，謁左宗棠，宗棠撫諭之。
units.en: He was soon recalled by order of the French minister; on taking leave of Zuo Zongtang, the latter treated him warmly.
units.literal: Soon he received orders from his minister to be relieved and return; he called on Zuo Zongtang, and Zongtang comforted and instructed him.

units.zh: 德克碑感服，願易服色受節度。
units.en: Deeply moved, von Sternberg agreed to change his uniform and serve under Chinese command.
units.literal: Von Sternberg was moved and submitted, willing to change his dress and accept command.

units.zh: 令駐守蕭山。
units.en: He was posted to garrison Xiaoshan.
units.literal: He was ordered to garrison Xiaoshan.

units.zh: 蔣益澧攻杭城，檄助戰，游擊何文秀攻雞籠山，德克碑從寶塔嶺登岸，攻倚城賊壘。
units.en: When Jiang Yili besieged Hangzhou, he was ordered to assist; Brigade Commander He Wenxiu attacked Jilong Hill while von Sternberg landed at Baota Ridge and assaulted the forts along the wall.
units.literal: Jiang Yili attacked Hangzhou city and ordered him to assist in the fighting; Brigade Commander He Wenxiu attacked Jilong Hill; von Sternberg landed from Baota Ridge and attacked the rebel forts leaning on the wall.

units.zh: 會天大霧，賊搆嘉興援賊自萬松嶺偪都司張誌公營，勢張甚。
units.en: A heavy fog fell; the rebels brought up Jiaxing reinforcements from Wansong Ridge and pressed Brigade Commander Zhang Zhigong's camp with great force.
units.literal: It happened that a great fog arose; the rebels drew in Jiaxing reinforcements from Wansong Ridge to press the camp of Brigade Commander Zhang Zhigong; their momentum was very strong.

units.zh: 德克碑率眾助擊，敗之。
units.en: Von Sternberg led his troops to the relief and routed them.
units.literal: Von Sternberg led his men to assist in the attack and defeated them.

units.zh: 益澧督水陸軍並進，連破九壘，令總兵高連升據其五，德克碑據其二，屯饅頭山。
units.en: Yili advanced land and naval forces together, captured nine forts in succession, gave five to Major General Gao Liansheng and two to von Sternberg, and encamped at Mantou Hill.
units.literal: Yili directed the land and water armies forward together, broke nine forts in succession, ordered Major General Gao Liansheng to hold five of them and von Sternberg to hold two, and encamped at Mantou Hill.

units.zh: 轟潰城數丈，毀鳳山門，官軍為承，城遂復。
units.en: They shelled several zhang of the wall, breached Fengshan Gate, the government troops pressed through, and the city was retaken.
units.literal: They blasted and breached several zhang of wall, destroyed Fengshan Gate, the government army followed up, and the city was recovered.

units.zh: 賊潰，奔湖州。
units.en: The rebels broke and fled toward Huzhou.
units.literal: The rebels were routed and fled to Huzhou.

units.zh: 攻安吉思溪，德克碑率所部助之，轟擊雙福橋，不克，駕小舟泊河汊，火八角亭，支木橋以濟。
units.en: In the attack on Anji and Jixi, von Sternberg supported the assault, shelled Shuangfu Bridge without success, then took a small boat up a creek, burned Bajiao Pavilion, and laid wooden bridges to cross.
units.literal: Attacking Anji and Jixi, von Sternberg led his unit to assist, shelled Shuangfu Bridge without success, drove a small boat to moor in a river fork, burned Bajiao Pavilion, and set up wooden bridges to cross.

units.zh: 賊阻兵中流不得進，德克碑賈勇偪岸，所部遇伏卻走，改趨荻港，越壕入，克三壘。
units.en: Rebels blocked the river and halted the advance; von Sternberg charged the bank boldly; his men hit an ambush and recoiled; he turned toward Dih Harbor, crossed the ditch, and took three forts.
units.literal: Rebels blocked the troops midstream so they could not advance; von Sternberg with fierce courage pressed the bank; his unit met an ambush and fell back; he changed direction toward Dih Harbor, crossed the moat and entered, and took three forts.

units.zh: 事寧，撤兵還上海。
units.en: When the campaign ended, his troops returned to Shanghai.
units.literal: When affairs were settled, the troops were withdrawn to Shanghai.

units.zh: 五年，充船政局副監督。
units.en: In 1866 he became deputy superintendent of the naval dockyard.
units.literal: In the fifth year he served as deputy superintendent of the naval dockyard.

units.zh: 七年，馬尾設船廠，督役興工，賞花翎。
units.en: In 1868 the Mawei shipyard was established; he oversaw construction and received the peacock feather.
units.literal: In the seventh year a shipyard was established at Mawei; he supervised the labor and began construction, and was awarded the peacock feather.

units.zh: 九年，宗棠平回亂，檄調甘肅，隸麾下。
units.en: In 1870, when Zuo pacified the northwestern Muslim revolts, he summoned von Sternberg to Gansu.
units.literal: In the ninth year Zongtang pacified the Muslim revolt in the northwest and ordered him transferred to Gansu under his command.

units.zh: 十三年，錄經始船政勞，膺獎賞。
units.en: In 1874 his services in founding the dockyard were recognized with an imperial reward.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, recording his merit in founding the dockyard, he received an award.

units.zh: 後卒。
units.en: He died some years later.
units.literal: Later he died.

units.zh: 赫德，字鷺賓，英國倍爾發司人。
units.en: Hart, courtesy name Lubin, was from Belfast in Britain.
units.literal: Hart, style name Lubin, was a native of Belfast in Britain.

units.zh: 咸豐四年，來中國，充寧波領事署繙譯官，調廣州。
units.en: He came to China in 1854 as interpreter at the Ningbo consulate and was later transferred to Guangzhou.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he came to China, served as interpreter in the Ningbo consulate, and was transferred to Guangzhou.

units.zh: 又充香港督署書記官。
units.en: He also served as clerk in the office of the governor of Hong Kong.
units.literal: He also served as clerk in the Hong Kong governor's office.

units.zh: 九年，改任粵海關副稅務司。
units.en: In 1859 he became deputy commissioner of the Canton Maritime Customs.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was made deputy commissioner of the Canton Maritime Customs.

units.zh: 十一年，總稅務司李泰國奉令購戰艦，以赫德權代之，赴長江新開各口岸置新關。
units.en: In 1861 Inspector General Lay was ordered to purchase warships; Hart acted for him and established customs houses at the newly opened Yangtze ports.
units.literal: In the eleventh year Inspector General Lay was ordered to purchase warships; Hart acted in his place and went to the newly opened Yangtze ports to establish new customs houses.

units.zh: 同治二年，李泰國去職，赫德實授，徙駐上海。
units.en: In 1863 Lay resigned and Hart was confirmed in the post, moving his headquarters to Shanghai.
units.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi Lay left office and Hart received formal appointment, moving his headquarters to Shanghai.

units.zh: 三年，置台灣南北新關。
units.en: In 1864 new customs houses were set up in northern and southern Taiwan.
units.literal: In the third year new customs houses were established in northern and southern Taiwan.

units.zh: 還駐京，加按察使銜。
units.en: He returned to Beijing and was given the rank of surveillance commissioner.
units.literal: He returned to be stationed in the capital and was given the rank of surveillance commissioner.

units.zh: 八年，晉布政使銜，赴緣海各地度置鐙樓塔表。
units.en: In 1869 he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner and toured the coast to establish lighthouses and navigation marks.
units.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner rank and went to coastal regions to survey and set up beacon towers and markers.

units.zh: 光緒二年，佐定砲台條約。
units.en: In 1876 he helped draft the Chefoo Convention provisions on forts.
units.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he assisted in drafting the fort treaty.

units.zh: 十年，赴金陵與法使議越南案。
units.en: In 1884 he went to Nanjing to negotiate the Tonkin affair with the French minister.
units.literal: In the tenth year he went to Jinling to negotiate the Annam case with the French minister.

units.zh: 會巡船置鐙樓台灣洋，為法虜，乃遣駐英稅務司金登幹赴巴黎申理，乘機與議停戰草約，還。
units.en: When a customs patrol boat erecting beacons off Taiwan was seized by France, he sent Commissioner Campbell to Paris to protest and negotiate a draft armistice.
units.literal: It happened that a patrol vessel setting up beacons in Taiwan waters was captured by France; he then sent Customs Commissioner Campbell in Britain to Paris to state the case, and took the opportunity to negotiate a draft armistice, then returned.

units.zh: 未幾，其國授為清、韓駐使，不就。
units.en: Britain soon offered him the post of minister to China and Korea, which he declined.
units.literal: Before long his country offered to appoint him minister to the Qing and Korea; he did not accept.

units.zh: 逾年，賞花翎、雙龍二等第一寶星。
units.en: The next year he received the peacock feather and the first-class Double Dragon Precious Star.
units.literal: The following year he was awarded the peacock feather and the first-class, second-grade Double Dragon Precious Star.

units.zh: 十二年，赴香港、澳門，條議洋藥稅釐並徵，並置關九龍、拱北。
units.en: In 1886 he went to Hong Kong and Macao to negotiate opium taxation and opened customs houses at Kowloon and Gongbei.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he went to Hong Kong and Macao to negotiate joint levies on foreign opium and established customs at Kowloon and Gongbei.

units.zh: 十三年，葡使來華，與訂澳門草約。
units.en: In 1887 he negotiated a draft Macao treaty with the Portuguese minister.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year the Portuguese minister came to China and he concluded a draft treaty on Macao with him.

units.zh: 十五年，藏兵寇哲孟雄，英兵乘勢闌入，赫德遣其弟稅務司赫政馳往，與駐藏大臣會籌劃界諸事。
units.en: In 1889, when Tibetan troops raided Sikkim and British forces intervened, Hart sent his brother Commissioner Hart to Tibet to negotiate the boundary with the resident commissioner.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year Tibetan troops raided Sikkim; British troops took advantage to intrude; Hart sent his younger brother, Customs Commissioner Hart junior, posthaste to confer with the resident commissioner in Tibet on boundary matters.

units.zh: 十九年，賞三代一品封典。
units.en: In 1893 he received the privilege of ennobling three generations at the first rank.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year he was granted the privilege of ennobling three generations with first rank.

units.zh: 二十五年，與德使籌置膠海新關。
units.en: In 1899 he worked with the German minister to establish customs at Jiaozhou Bay.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he negotiated with the German minister to establish the new Jiaozhou customs.

units.zh: 明年，各國聯軍入京，贊襄和議，晉太子少保。
units.en: The following year, when the allied armies entered Beijing, he assisted in the peace talks and was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: The next year the allied armies of various countries entered the capital; he assisted in the peace negotiations and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 二十八年，召入覲，賜「福」字。
units.en: In 1902 he was received in audience and granted the character Fu, "blessing."
units.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was summoned to audience and granted the character "Fu" (blessing).

units.zh: 三十一年，與德使更議膠關章程，改行無稅區地法。
units.en: In 1905 he renegotiated the Jiaozhou customs regulations with Germany, adopting a duty-free zone.
units.literal: In the thirty-first year he renegotiated with the German minister the regulations for the Jiaozhou customs and changed to the duty-free zone system.

units.zh: 尋與日使籌置大連灣新關，徵榷一如膠海。
units.en: He soon negotiated the Dalian customs with Japan on the same terms as Jiaozhou.
units.literal: Soon he negotiated with the Japanese minister to establish the new Dalian customs, with taxation the same as at Jiaozhou.

units.zh: 三十三年，東三省度地置關。
units.en: In 1907 he surveyed the northeast and established customs there.
units.literal: In the thirty-third year he surveyed land in the three eastern provinces and established customs.

units.zh: 逾年，謝病歸，詔許之，加尚書銜。
units.en: The next year he resigned on grounds of illness; the throne granted leave and gave him ministerial rank.
units.literal: The following year he asked leave on grounds of illness to return home; the edict permitted it and he was given ministerial rank.

units.zh: 赫德官中國垂五十年，頗與士大夫往還。
units.en: Hart served in China for nearly fifty years and moved widely in scholarly and official circles.
units.literal: Hart held office in China for nearly fifty years and associated considerably with scholar-officials.

units.zh: 嘗教其子習製藝文，擬應試，未許。
units.en: He once taught his son the examination essay in hope he might sit for the civil examinations, but the court would not allow it.
units.literal: He once taught his son the examination essay style, intending him to sit for the civil service examinations, but permission was not granted.

units.zh: 總署嘗擬請授總海防司，道員薛福成以其陰鷙專利，常內西人而外中國，上書鴻章力爭之，議始寢。
units.en: The Zongli Yamen once proposed making him director general of coastal defense; Circuit Intendant Xue Fucheng, who regarded him as secretive, self-interested, and partial to the West against China, protested vigorously to Li Hongzhang and the plan was abandoned.
units.literal: The Zongli Yamen once proposed appointing him Director General of Coastal Defense; Circuit Intendant Xue Fucheng, considering him secretive and self-seeking, always siding with Westerners against China, memorialized Hongzhang and argued forcefully against it, and the proposal was dropped.

units.zh: 辛亥後，病卒，賜優恤。
units.en: After the 1911 revolution he died of illness and received generous posthumous honors.
units.literal: After the Xinhai year he died of illness, and generous posthumous favor was granted.

units.zh: 帛黎，法國人。
units.en: Brière was French.
units.literal: Brière was a Frenchman.

units.zh: 同治八年，來中國，充福州船政學校教員。
units.en: He came to China in 1869 as an instructor at the Foochow Naval College.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Tongzhi he came to China and served as an instructor at the Foochow Naval College.

units.zh: 十二年，賞五品銜，予雙龍獎牌。
units.en: In 1873 he received fifth rank and the Double Dragon medal.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he was awarded fifth rank and given the Double Dragon medal.

units.zh: 明年，調充江海關稅務幫辦，歷鎮江、北海、甌海、臨海、粵海諸關。
units.en: The following year he became assistant commissioner at Shanghai and served at Zhenjiang, Beihai, Wenzhou, Linhai, and Canton.
units.literal: The next year he was transferred as assistant in the Shanghai customs, serving successively at Zhenjiang, Beihai, Ouhai, Linhai, and Yuehai customs.

units.zh: 光緒十九年，晉三品銜，調北京，遷稅務司。
units.en: In 1893 he was promoted to third rank, transferred to Beijing, and appointed customs commissioner.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year of Guangxu he was promoted to third rank, transferred to Beijing, and made customs commissioner.

units.zh: 二十二年，朝議行郵政，以赫德兼領其事，帛黎實參治之。
units.en: In 1896 the court decided to establish a postal service; Hart nominally headed it while Brière ran the operation.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year the court debated instituting a postal service; Hart was placed in overall charge, and Brière actually administered it.

units.zh: 凡都會、省城、通商口岸，漸次置局，命曰「大清郵政」。
units.en: Post offices called "Great Qing Post" were opened in every capital, provincial seat, and treaty port.
units.literal: In every metropolis, provincial capital, and treaty port, offices were gradually established, named the "Great Qing Post."

units.zh: 尋徙拱北。
units.en: He was soon transferred to Gongbei.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Gongbei.

units.zh: 二十六年，還京。
units.en: In 1900 he returned to Beijing.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he returned to the capital.

units.zh: 明年，遷郵政總辦，晉二品銜。
units.en: The following year he became director general of the postal service with second rank.
units.literal: The next year he was made director general of the postal service and promoted to second rank.

units.zh: 置代辦局於蕪湖​​。
units.en: He set up an agency office at Wuhu.
units.literal: He established an agency office at Wuhu.

units.zh: 二十九年，河南、山東、山西、貴州復置副總局，自是內地城鄉村鎮，街郵遍設。
units.en: In 1903 sub-head offices opened in Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, and Guizhou, and rural post routes spread across the interior.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year sub-head offices were again established in Henan, Shandong, Shanxi, and Guizhou; from then on postal routes spread through inland cities, towns, and villages.

units.zh: 時尚未入萬國郵政公會，即已與日本及英屬印度、香港聯約試行。
units.en: Though not yet in the Universal Postal Union, China already had trial agreements with Japan, British India, and Hong Kong.
units.literal: Although China had not yet entered the Universal Postal Union, trial agreements were already made with Japan and with British India and Hong Kong.

units.zh: 三十年，賞雙龍三等第一寶星。
units.en: In 1904 he received the third-class Double Dragon Precious Star.
units.literal: In the thirtieth year he was awarded the third-class, first-grade Double Dragon Precious Star.

units.zh: 與法、德及英屬那達商定聯郵章程。
units.en: He concluded joint postal regulations with France, Germany, and British Natal.
units.literal: He agreed on joint postal regulations with France, Germany, and British Nada.

units.zh: 先後成郵政六百餘局，代辦四千二百餘所。
units.en: He established more than six hundred post offices and over four thousand two hundred agencies.
units.literal: In all, more than six hundred post offices and more than four thousand two hundred agency stations were established.

units.zh: 宣統三年，改隸郵傳部，設總局，尚書盛宣懷疏薦之，遂被命為總辦，郵局置官自此始。
units.en: In 1911 the service passed to the Ministry of Posts; Minister Sheng Xuanhuai recommended Brière as director general, and the post office first received a formal Chinese bureaucracy.
units.literal: In the third year of Xuantong it was placed under the Ministry of Posts and Communications; a head office was set up; Minister Sheng Xuanhuai memorialized recommending him, and he was appointed director general; from this the postal service first received official staffing.

units.zh: 越二年，乞病歸。
units.en: Two years later he resigned for illness and returned home.
units.literal: After two years he begged leave on grounds of illness to return home.

units.zh: 未幾，卒。
units.en: He died soon after.
units.literal: Before long he died.

units.zh: 論曰：華爾、戈登先後領常勝軍，立功江、浙，世稱「洋將」，時傳其戰略。
units.en: The commentators observe: Ward and Gordon led the Ever Victorious Army in turn, won fame in Jiangsu and Zhejiang as "foreign generals," and their tactics were widely discussed.
units.literal: The commentators say: Ward and Gordon successively led the Ever Victorious Army, won merit in Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and the age called them "foreign generals"; their battle plans were widely circulated.

units.zh: 日意格初亦參防戰，繼以船政著勞。
units.en: Giquel first fought in the defense of the coast, then earned lasting credit at the naval dockyard.
units.literal: Giquel at first also took part in defense and fighting, and later won distinction through the naval dockyard.

units.zh: 赫德久總稅務，兼司郵政，頗與聞交涉，號曰「客卿」，皆能不負所事。
units.en: Hart long controlled the customs and postal service, took part in diplomacy, and was known as a "guest minister"; each served faithfully.
units.literal: Hart long headed the customs and also managed the postal service; he was much involved in diplomacy and was called a "guest minister"; all fulfilled their duties without failing their charge.

units.zh: 茲數人者，受官職，易冠服，或原隸國籍。
units.en: These men accepted Chinese office, adopted Chinese dress, or had begun in foreign service.
units.literal: These several men accepted official posts, changed their dress, or had originally entered foreign service.

units.zh: 食其祿者忠其事，實有足多，故並著於篇。
units.en: Those who draw a salary should be loyal to their charge; they deserved praise, and are therefore recorded together in this chapter.
units.literal: Those who eat a state's salary should be loyal to its affairs; they truly had much to commend, and therefore are all recorded in this chapter.
